issues.legal_issue: An arbitrator does not commit misconduct by making a challenged ruling on a claim of privilege where the ruling was made during the proceedings, the party did not press for a decision to enable further evidence, and no resulting prejudice is shown.
material_facts: The appellant alleged that the arbitrator had not ruled on the respondents’ claim of privilege when he said he did and had later inserted the order into the record.
The arbitrator and another witness testified that the order had been pronounced on the date it bore, while witnesses for the appellant disputed that account.
The appellant had argued the privilege issue but did not ask the arbitrator to decide it before the award so that it could produce secondary evidence if necessary.
The documents concerned the meaning of “provisional” in the cattle pricing arrangements and were not shown to have caused the appellant injustice or prevented it from producing further evidence.
The lower courts rejected the allegation of misconduct, and the Supreme Court declined to disturb their concurrent findings.
issues.conclusion: The arbitrator was not guilty of misconduct in relation to the privilege ruling, and the appellant had waived any objection to the manner in which that evidentiary issue was handled.
issues.legal_principle: An objection to an arbitrator’s decision about admitting evidence may be waived like other objections to the conduct of the proceedings; a party may not wait until an unfavorable award and then seek to set it aside on a procedural objection it did not pursue during the arbitration. The Court cited Russell on Arbitration, Seventeenth Edition, page 182; it relied on no statutory provision for this ruling.

rule.if: arbitration_award_challenge_appeal and privilege_ruling_challenged and objection_not_pressed_during_arbitration and no_prejudice_from_privilege_ruling

predicates.arbitration_award_challenge_appeal: A party appeals from a decision upholding an arbitration award.
predicates.privilege_ruling_challenged: A party alleges that the arbitrator mishandled a ruling on a claim of privilege over evidence.
predicates.objection_not_pressed_during_arbitration: The party did not pursue the objection during the arbitration in order to obtain a ruling or take further steps to present evidence.
predicates.no_prejudice_from_privilege_ruling: The challenged ruling did not prevent the party from presenting evidence or otherwise cause it injustice.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an arbitration award over a privilege ruling, the arbitrator is not treated as having committed misconduct if the objection was not pursued during the arbitration and the ruling caused no prejudice.

issues.legal_issue: An arbitrator’s interpretation of an agreement is not open to challenge when the parties submit their claims on the agreement alone and the dispute turns on its meaning.
material_facts: The appellant’s claims were based on the agreement, and its written argument stated that the parties relied on the agreement and nothing else.
The dispute included the meaning of “provisional” in the stated prices of certain cattle and the appellant’s claim for depreciation.
The appellant argued that “provisional” meant depreciation should be allowed and that the final cost would be lower.

The agreement’s wording did not necessarily mean that the final figure would be lower, and the record contained evidence relevant to the actual book values and the appellant’s depreciation calculations.
issues.conclusion: The arbitrator’s decision on the interpretation of the agreement was not open to challenge, and the appellant was not entitled to relief on its depreciation claim based on the word “provisional.”
issues.legal_principle: Where the parties confine their claims to an agreement and the arbitrator must decide its effect, the decision is one of law concerning interpretation of the document and is not open to challenge. The Court relied on Durga Prosad v. Sewkishendas and Ghulam Jilani v. Muhammad Hassan (1901) 29 Ind App 51 (PC); it cited no statutory provision for this ruling.

predicates.arbitration_award_challenge_appeal: A party appeals from a decision upholding an arbitration award.
predicates.claims_confined_to_written_agreement: The parties base their claims on the written agreement alone, rather than on other assurances or arrangements.
predicates.dispute_requires_interpreting_agreement: The arbitrator must determine the meaning or effect of the agreement to resolve the dispute.

issues.definition: When an arbitration appeal concerns an interpretation that the parties submitted on the written agreement alone, the arbitrator’s interpretation is not open to challenge.

issues.legal_issue: An arbitrator may decide a dispute about returning land when the land issue is included in the parties’ claims and counterclaim, even if the agreement has not been terminated.
material_facts: The appellant itself asked the arbitrator to direct that land be conveyed to it.

The agreement made land available for growing fodder and other food for the cattle, set a limit by reference to the number of cattle, and required land to be relinquished if cattle numbers fell short.
The evidence showed that the appellant used the land to raise cash crops rather than the stipulated fodder crops.
The respondents sought return of the land in their counterclaim because of that use, and the return of the land was also addressed in the parties’ claims and arguments.
The appellant’s argument that return could not be ordered because the agreement had not been terminated was raised only in its special leave petition.
issues.conclusion: The arbitrator was competent to make an award on the return of the land.
issues.legal_principle: The arbitrator’s authority extended to a matter raised in the parties’ claims and counterclaim; the appellant’s own request concerning the land and the respondents’ claim for its return placed the matter before the arbitrator. The Court relied on the agreement’s terms and the scope of the parties’ submissions, and cited no statutory provision or earlier case for this ruling.

predicates.arbitration_award_challenge_appeal: A party appeals from a decision upholding an arbitration award.
predicates.land_issue_included_in_parties_claims: The parties’ claims or counterclaim place the land’s transfer or return before the arbitrator.
predicates.land_use_breached_agreed_purpose: The party in possession uses the land for a purpose other than the purpose stipulated in the agreement.

issues.definition: If an arbitration appeal concerns land that the parties placed before the arbitrator and the land was used contrary to its agreed purpose, the arbitrator is competent to decide whether it must be returned.

issues.legal_issue: An allegation that an arbitrator was influenced by a public official’s speech does not invalidate an award when the allegation is rejected as having no substance.
material_facts: The appellant alleged that the arbitrator had been influenced by a speech in which the then Chief Minister accused the society of mismanagement.
The courts below rejected this contention, and the Supreme Court accepted their conclusion that it had no substance.
issues.conclusion: The allegation that the speech influenced the arbitrator provided no basis for disturbing the award.
issues.legal_principle: The Court accepted the lower courts’ conclusion that the allegation had no substance. The judgment states no separate statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this ruling.

predicates.arbitration_award_challenge_appeal: A party appeals from a decision upholding an arbitration award.
predicates.public_speech_influence_alleged: A party alleges that a public official’s speech influenced the arbitrator.
predicates.lower_courts_rejected_influence_allegati: The lower courts conclude that the allegation of influence has no substance.

issues.definition: When an arbitration appeal relies on an alleged influence from a public official’s speech and the lower courts have rejected that allegation as insubstantial, the award is not invalidated on that ground.
